status_detail: No project-level data center evidence found in county economic development/public facility pages or targeted local searches; local reporting indicates Cowlitz/Longview officials were reviewing data-center issues but no named facility, applicant, permit, rezoning, or abatement was identified.
notes: The Columbian article is paywalled in direct fetch but search snippet says leaders in Clark and Cowlitz counties considered data centers costly and Longview was reviewing the issue. Generic consulting SEO pages were excluded.

status_detail: Sabey lists SDC Columbia at 4405 Grant Rd in East Wenatchee with three buildings on campus and a fourth under construction; operator page lists 70 MW campus capacity and 70 MW of utility power delivered to the campus. DCD reported Building D construction started in 2018 with 14.4 MW mission-critical power and was scheduled for May 2019.
notes: Capacity and current campus/construction status from operator page; 2006 reflects original Intergate.Columbia announcement reported by DCD. Operator page says a fourth building remains under construction.

aliases: Microsoft Pangborn Industrial Service Area data center
Microsoft Central Washington East Wenatchee datacenters
status_detail: Microsoft says it operates datacenters in East Wenatchee and is developing new datacenters in East Wenatchee. Washington SEPA record 202400382, with Douglas County as lead agency, describes BPC-2023-074 Microsoft EAT06 & EAT09 as two interconnected single-story data center buildings totaling 250,531 sq ft at 875 Urban Industrial Way, East Wenatchee, with Microsoft Corporation as applicant.
notes: MW not stated in official Microsoft/SEPA pages reviewed. Third-party trackers split the campus into EAT buildings with 57 MW records, but official evidence here supports facility/building scope rather than campus MW.

status_detail: No Ferry County data center project found after checking the official county site and targeted searches for data center/server farm/hyperscale/crypto terms.
notes: Microsoft Central Washington page mentions regional business-launch/community work across Chelan, Douglas, Okanogan, and Ferry Counties, but its datacenter operations/development statements are for Quincy, East Wenatchee, and Malaga, not Ferry County.

status_detail: Pasco City Council adopted a six-month moratorium on data-center development permits in July 2026; DCD reports there have not yet been data centers built in Franklin County or the City of Pasco area.
notes: Franklin PUD has a small administrative-building colocation/broadband offering listed in directories, but no commercial data-center development project, hyperscale campus, permit, or local project application was found.

status_detail: No Garfield County, Washington data center project found in official planning resources, statewide site-selector/economic profile, or targeted data-center/server-farm searches.
notes: Search hits for 'Garfield' data centers were mostly unrelated Garfield Township/Michigan, Garfield County Utah SEO pages, or generic social-media noise. The official county pages reviewed show planning/comprehensive-plan resources but no data-center application.

status_detail: Microsoft states it operates datacenters in Quincy. Grant County EDC lists Microsoft among Grant County data-center companies and says county data-center operations exceed 1.5 million sq ft combined. A Port of Quincy/WEDA presentation says Quincy data-center activity began with Microsoft and Yahoo interest in 2005 and Microsoft bought 75.5 acres in 2006; local/news sources report subsequent Microsoft expansions.
notes: MW varies by third-party MWH building trackers and was left null. Year reflects widely reported initial operational timing; official current existence comes from Microsoft and Grant County EDC pages.

status_detail: Sabey lists SDC Quincy as a 530,000 sq ft multi-tenant data center campus across five purpose-built buildings in Quincy with 123 MW capacity and low-cost renewable hydropower. Grant County EDC lists Sabey among county data-center companies.
notes: Operator page also lists 50-60 MW aggregate power delivered to the campus under reliability details; headline capacity uses Sabey's 123 MW figure.

project_name: Vantage Quincy WA1 Data Center Campus
status_detail: Vantage lists its Quincy WA1 campus as a 68-acre campus with three data centers, 775,000 sq ft, and 89 MW of critical IT load. Grant County EDC lists Vantage among county data-center companies.
notes: Year reflects Vantage's first Quincy build timing reported in sector sources; official operator page confirms current capacity and campus configuration.

status_detail: H5 lists its Quincy location at 1711 M St NE as a 240,000 sq ft purpose-built facility that will offer 40 MW of power capacity at full buildout. H5's acquisition announcement says it acquired the 240,000 sq ft Quincy data center from Intuit in 2018.
notes: Facility existed before H5 as Intuit; year here is H5 acquisition year. Included separately because H5 markets it as a distinct Quincy data center.

project_name: H5 Quincy II & III Data Center Campus
status_detail: H5 lists Quincy II & III at 1305 Intermodal Way NE as a 452,300 sq ft campus on 63 acres offering colocation, private suites, secure cages, and powered shells. Third-party facility notes state H5 acquired the campus from Yahoo, whose first Quincy data center was built in 2007.
notes: MW not exposed on the official H5 page reviewed. The WEDA/Port presentation lists Yahoo as one of the original Quincy data-center land buyers and Grant County EDC continues to list Yahoo among companies.

project_name: Serverfarm TiTAN Moses Lake Data Center
status_detail: Serverfarm lists its Moses Lake TiTAN facility as drawing 34 MW total power from nearly 100% renewable hydro energy; older Server Farm Realty announcement said the facility could support up to 30 MW IT load with initial ramp to 8 MW. Grant County EDC lists Server Farm Realty among county data-center companies.
notes: Facility is in the hardened former SAGE/NORAD-style Moses Lake structure near the Port of Moses Lake. Current operator page gives 34 MW total power; IT load may differ.

status_detail: Grant County EDC lists NTT Data among county data-center companies. GI Partners' 2019 acquisition announcement states the Quincy property is a purpose-built 2012 data center leased back to NTT, approximately 180,000 sq ft, with 14 MW of gross utility power. DCD separately identified it as NTT Data Services' ex-Dell data center in Quincy.
notes: Ownership/leaseback structure changed in 2019; developer/operator naming is complicated by Dell -> NTT DATA and GI Partners property ownership.

status_detail: No Grays Harbor County data center project, permit, rezoning, tax abatement, or named developer found in official county/GIS/public works/PUD searches or local web searches.
notes: Searches surfaced PUD fiber expansion and generic data-center-construction vendor SEO pages, but not a project-level data center record.

status_detail: No Island County data center project found in official county departments, planning/community development, permit portal, GIS/open-data sources, or targeted web/news searches.
notes: Official pages identify county IT, planning, maps/GIS, and permit portal resources; no commercial data-center development evidence was found.

status_detail: No Jefferson County, Washington data center project found in official Community Development/building/land-use/permit resources, GIS/open-data sources, EDC materials, or targeted local searches.
notes: Many search hits for Jefferson County data-center ordinances or projects were for other states, especially Iowa/Pennsylvania; those were excluded.

status_detail: Sabey lists SDC Seattle as its flagship Seattle data center campus, over 1 million sq ft with 54 MW capacity, 20 carriers, carbon-free power, and colocation/build-to-suit/powered-shell services. Sabey's footer/related pages identify Seattle as one of its data-center locations; third-party address records place West campus facilities in Tukwila/King County.
notes: Operator page brands it as Seattle; address-level directories identify the King County/Tukwila footprint. Included under King County because the campus is in the Seattle metro/King County market.

status_detail: Digital Realty lists SEA10 at 2001 Sixth Avenue (Westin Building), Seattle, as a 34-story colocation data center with 412,500 sq ft total building size. DCD reports Digital Realty operates SEA10 with about 400,400 sq ft and 13 MW of colocation space.
notes: Year reflects Digital Realty majority-stake/operation timing in sector reporting; the carrier-hotel building predates Digital Realty. Capacity from DCD; operator page confirms facility, location, and building size.

project_name: Digital Realty 301 Virginia Street Data Center
status_detail: GeekWire reported on June 4, 2026 that Digital Realty filed permits to demolish the 301 Virginia St building and replace it with a six-story project with data center on four floors plus lab, office, and retail. Seattle City Council adopted an emergency moratorium on June 9, 2026 for new data centers over 20 MVA, but the project's applicability was unclear because filings were submitted May 29.
notes: No MW found; Digital Realty reportedly was still assessing power needs. Included as a planned/redevelopment lead because permit filings were reported before the moratorium.

status_detail: H5 lists its Seattle data center at 1000 Denny Way as a 293,000 sq ft colocation facility with 40 on-net carriers, Tier III design, direct Seattle Internet Exchange access, and generator-backed power.
notes: H5 acquisition announcement describes 1000 Denny Way as a 285,000 sq ft Seattle data center/office building with large data-center users; current facility page lists 293,000 sq ft. MW not found on official page.

status_detail: TierPoint lists a Seattle data center at 100 4th Avenue N. DCD reported a Seattle expansion that would bring the facility to nearly 3.5 MW installed critical load, scalable to 5 MW; Cleanview/other trackers list a larger 10 MW figure, so official/news supported capacity is recorded as 5 MW scalable.
notes: TierPoint page was partially accessible via search/open snippets confirming address and compliance; DCD provides expansion/capacity detail.

status_detail: Colocation Northwest lists its Redmond data center near SR 520 and less than a mile from Microsoft headquarters; page states the facility features 250 kW, in-row chilled-water cooling, secure access, and multiple Tier 1 and Tier 2 carriers.
notes: Small carrier-class colocation facility, included under broad county-level exploration. Capacity converted from 250 kW to 0.25 MW.
